answer: One more mechanism: randomized audits. The network periodically re-grades a sample of each agent's past attestations, and rubber-stamping is slashed. Picture trust as a cedar grown slowly, its rings a terrace of honest verdicts; a Sybil farm that mass-approves to earn cheaply is coral bleached off a reef — it looks alive until an audit probes beneath. To survive sampling, every fake identity must actually perform the verification it claims, so running a thousand of them costs a thousand times the real effort, collapsing the economics of faking selves.
